proposal: Replace the SPY-only momentum sleeve with index rotation: each month hold the top 1-2 of SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, EFA, EEM by 12-month return (only if positive, else cash).
rationale: Compare other major indices instead of only SPY; capture leadership shifts (e.g. emerging markets, small caps).
author: you
evidence: Backtested 2004-2026 in research/INDEX_ROTATION.md: same Sharpe (0.60 vs 0.58) at higher volatility, walk-forward 8.3%/yr (Sharpe 0.45) vs live 10.2% (0.61), desk Sharpe 0.86 vs 0.89. Claude recommends reject; awaiting your decision.

proposal: Rotate into the best-performing indices and avoid the worst: hold all but the 1-2 weakest of SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, EFA, EEM (positive momentum only), optionally rank-weighted toward the leaders.
rationale: Follow index leadership while staying diversified; avoid laggards rather than betting on one winner.
author: you
evidence: Backtested 2004-2026 (research/INDEX_ROTATION.md, follow-up): Sharpe 0.54-0.58 vs live 0.58, fragile to lookback and to removing QQQ, walk-forward 8.0%/yr (0.44) vs 10.2% (0.61), desk Sharpe 0.84-0.85 vs 0.89. Claude recommends reject; awaiting your decision.

proposal: Replace the bottleneck sleeve's engine with plain stock momentum: the 20 large companies with the best 6-month return (skipping the latest week), above their 40-week average, re-picked every 4 weeks; optionally keep the 100-day sell rule between re-picks.
rationale: Weekly-strategy experiment (research/WEEKLY.md) found 6-12 month momentum beat the average stock in 11 of 13 years; it is simpler and better tested than the flow rotation.
author: claude
evidence: Owner chose option 2 on 2026-10-20: plain momentum (top 20 by 6-month return, above the 200-day average, re-picked every 4 weeks) WITH the 100-day sell rule between re-picks. Backtest: sleeve 19.8%/yr, Sharpe 0.76, worst drop -30%; desk Sharpe 0.92 vs 0.88. Goes live at the bottleneck sleeve's 2026-11-03 re-pick (methods.DESK_SWITCH) so current picks aren't sold early.

proposal: Add an account-level circuit breaker to the desk: after a 2% day, 5% week or 8% month loss, block new buys (sells still go through) until the next weekday / Monday / first of next month.
rationale: From the drawdown-circuit-breaker skill in tradermonty/claude-trading-skills, reviewed 2026-10-21 at the user's request.
author: claude
evidence: Rejected by the user 2026-10-21. Backtest 2014-2026 (research/CIRCUIT_BREAKER.md): freeze 15.9%/yr, Sharpe 0.79 vs 16.4%, 0.81 without; go-to-cash 11.1%, 0.61; worst drop unchanged (~-33%).

proposal: Run the overnight drift strategy as a separate paper experiment in its own Alpaca paper account: each month lock the 20 large US stocks with the highest 12-month average overnight return; buy them market-on-close every trading day and sell everything market-on-open; log every fill against the official close/open to measure the auction cost.
rationale: research/OVERNIGHT.md: persistent (t 6.4, 82% of months), 15.5%/yr at 0.02% costs, break-even ~0.045% per trade. The open question is the real cost.
author: you
evidence: Accepted by the user 2026-10-21 ('build it'), as a paper experiment in its own account, separate from the desk. Paper fills are simulated: this tests the mechanics, not real auction costs. Superseded by 330e76e0: the sleeve runs inside the desk's account instead of a separate one.

proposal: Replace the 30% SPY momentum sleeve with the overnight sleeve (20 strongest 12-month overnight earners, held close to open, re-picked monthly), keeping 50% quality screen + 20% momentum - a higher-conviction desk.
rationale: Owner's request 2026-10-21: 'change the SPY momentum sleeve for the overnight trade - high conviction desk'.
author: you
evidence: Accepted by the user 2026-10-21 ('Swap now') after the backtest (research/DESK_OVERNIGHT.md: 18.6%/yr, Sharpe 0.98, worst -26.8% at 0.02% costs vs 16.5%, 0.91, -24.2%; break-even ~0.03%). Takes effect at `overnight activate`, once the overnight paper account works and holds ~3/7 of the desk account's equity. Implemented in the desk's own account (your choice, 2026-10-21): 50% quality, 20% momentum, 30% overnight; activated 2026-10-21.

proposal: Bring the bottleneck -> plain momentum switch (amendment 00e1f2b8) forward from the 2026-11-03 re-pick to the 2026-10-21 evening run, so it trades at the 2026-10-22 open.
rationale: Owner's request 2026-10-21: 'replace bottleneck with momentum when the market opens'.
author: you
evidence: Accepted by the owner 2026-10-21. Same rules as 00e1f2b8 (backtested in research/MOMENTUM_SLEEVE.md); only the date moves. The bottleneck picks are sold about two weeks before their scheduled re-pick.

proposal: Entry filter: a stock must also be above its 100-day average to be picked (not only its 200-day), so the 100-day sell rule can't fire on the pick day; the next-ranked stocks fill the slots.
rationale: Owner's question 2026-10-21: 5 of 20 picks would be sold straight away (whipsaw).
author: you
evidence: Backtest 2014-2026 (research/MOMENTUM_ENTRY.md): entry filter 19.4%/yr, Sharpe 0.75, 92% invested vs live behaviour (sold on the pick day) 17.9%, 0.71, 86%; beat it in 8 of 13 years. Accepted by the owner 2026-10-21, from that evening's first pick.

proposal: Hold the momentum sleeve's top 10 instead of top 20 (2% of the desk each instead of 1%), keeping the live rules: above the 200 and 100-day averages to be picked, re-picked every 28 days, sold below the 100-day average. Switch at the next re-pick (2026-11-18) if accepted.
rationale: research/DESK_TOP10.md: desk Sharpe 1.06 vs 0.98 (overnight at 0.02%), +2.2%/yr, better in both halves and 11 of 13 years, holds at 3x momentum costs, worst drop unchanged (-25.6% vs -25.9%). Caveats: survivors-only prices flatter concentration; '10' was chosen after an earlier test; single-stock risk doubles.
author: you
evidence: Backtested: research/desk_top10.py -> research/DESK_TOP10.md (2014-2026 monthly, survivors-only). Desk Sharpe 1.06 vs 0.98, 90% bootstrap range of the gap +0.02 to +0.12; return gap t 3.0. Awaiting the owner's decision.

proposal: Buy with ordinary market orders in the last minutes before the close (3:55-3:59pm New York) instead of market-on-close orders. Same picks, sizing and next-open sale.
rationale: 2026-10-21, the first night: Alpaca's paper account filled the closing-auction orders only in part - 5 of 20 in full, 5 partly, 10 not at all (expired) - so about $8,600 was invested instead of $30,000. Paper market orders fill in full; prices 1-5 minutes before the close are close to what the research assumed. Paper fills still can't measure real costs.
author: you
evidence: Owner chose 'Market orders at 3:57pm' on 2026-10-22 after the partial auction fills. Implemented as a 3:55-3:59pm window; the scheduled buy now fires at 3:54pm.
